subject: Clarifying keystore/operator scope for private deployment (VPC/on-prem)
messages:
From: Serena Holt <serena.holt@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: BluePeak Legal <contracts@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy keystore/ops questions for DPA

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we evaluate Redwood for a private VPC deployment, our security and legal teams have a short list of clarifications before we sign the DPA and proceed with an on-prem pilot. Key items:

- Customer-held keys: we require that our master keys remain in our KMS (Azure Key Vault) and that Redwood operate only with wrapped keys. We need a clear operator access matrix showing if/when Redwood engineers can unwrap or rotate keys.
- Operator (break-glass) access: under what circumstances would Redwood operators have the ability to decrypt customer data? We need a list of triggers, approval workflows, and audit evidence.
- Subprocessors: a complete list of subprocessors that may touch metadata, logs, or support bundles in a private deployment (including cloud partners, monitoring vendors, or ticketing systems).
- Cross-border transfer risk: although our primary region is US, we need assurances on data residency for support artifacts and any automated telemetry.

I've attached BluePeak's security checklist for your reference. Can you ask your engineering and legal teams to provide an operator-keystore responsibilities matrix and a short summary of the support workflow (including who signs off on break-glass events)?

Best,

Serena Holt
Head of Information Security
BluePeak Health
Attachment: bluepeak_security_requirements_2028.pdf
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Serena Holt <serena.holt@bluepeakhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy keystore/ops questions for DPA

Hi Serena — thanks for the checklist, very helpful. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Marcus (Ops) to put together concrete artifacts. Quick answers up front:

- Keystore model: Redwood supports a customer-controlled KMS model for VPC and on-prem. We never persist unwrapped customer master keys in our control plane. We can maintain wrapped model keys and provide APIs for customer-initiated rotations.
- Break-glass: by default, Redwood engineers do not have the ability to decrypt customer data. Break-glass requires a documented request, at least two authorized approvers from the customer, and on-call approval from our security lead. Every break-glass action generates immutable audit records.
- Subprocessors: for private deployments we limit subprocessors and can provide a tailored list; some monitoring/logging components may be vendor-hosted depending on the deployment model.

Will follow up with the matrix and a short procedural doc by Thursday.

— Lukas
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Serena Holt <serena.holt@bluepeakhealth.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Aug 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Operator-keystore responsibilities matrix (draft)

Hi Serena — attaching a first-pass matrix and a short runbook describing support interactions for VPC and on-prem installs. Highlights:

- Key custody: customer holds the root CMK in Azure Key Vault. Redwood receives wrapped KEKs and uses a local hardware enclave (on dedicated nodes) to perform transient unwrapping only during model load; no unwrapped keys are written to persistent storage.
- Support bundle handling: support bundles may include redacted logs and non-sensitive telemetry. We offer an option to deliver bundles directly to the customer's S3/Blob storage; default is a time-bound, encrypted transfer to our support tenant that is subject to customer approval.
- Break-glass workflow: request -> customer approval (2 approvers) -> Redwood security on-call -> temporary access token; all actions logged.

Attachments included: redwood_keystore_responsibilities_v1.xlsx (matrix) and runbook excerpt. Let us know what needs tightening.

-Marcus
Senior Cloud Ops Engineer
Attachment: redwood_keystore_responsibilities_v1.xlsx
From: Serena Holt <serena.holt@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: BluePeak Legal <contracts@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Aug 2028 10:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator-keystore responsibilities matrix (draft)

Marcus — thanks for the draft. A few pointed follow-ups from our side:

1) Enclave details: Can you confirm the attestation model and whether we can require Intel SGX attestation reports or equivalent? We will want to include attestation as part of the acceptance criteria.
2) Support bundle redaction: we need explicit fields that will always be removed (PHI fields in logs, patient IDs). Can Redwood provide a pre-filter to sanitize before any transfer to Redwood systems?
3) Subprocessor list: please provide names/locations and purpose (e.g., PagerDuty — US — incident routing). If a monitoring vendor is used, we will want contractual flow-down obligations in the DPA addendum.

Our legal team is preparing redlines to your DPA and will share by COB Monday.

-Serena
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: BluePeak Legal <contracts@bluepeakhealth.com>, Serena Holt <serena.holt@bluepeakhealth.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Aug 2028 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed DPA additions and subprocessor disclosure

Hi Serena and BluePeak Legal —

Attached is our proposed DPA addendum (redwood_dpa_proposed_v3.docx) and an explicit subprocessor register for private deployments. Summary of concessions and next steps:

- Keystore custody: we accept language that customers retain sole custody of CMKs and that Redwood will only use wrapped key material; proposed clause in section 2.3.
- Attestation: we can commit to providing attestation reports (SGX or equivalent) on demand during onboarding and after major infra changes; we propose quarterly attestation snapshots for enterprise customers.
- Support bundle policy: new clause adding customer-controlled delivery: support bundles will be delivered to customer-managed storage by default unless customer opts into Redwood-hosted troubleshooting.
- Subprocessors: attached register lists vendors and country of processing. Any additions will be pre-notified 30 days and subject to customer objection rights for high-risk processors.

Please review the DPA addendum and let us know any edits; Kimberly and I can hop on a call with BluePeak Legal tomorrow if helpful.

Regards,

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_dpa_proposed_v3.docx
From: Victor Ramos <victor.ramos@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Serena Holt <serena.holt@bluepeakhealth.com>, BluePeak Legal <contracts@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed DPA additions and subprocessor disclosure

Kimberly — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifications from contracts/security:

- The 30-day pre-notification for subprocessors is fine, but we need the right to reject any new processor that will persist patient-identifiable metadata. Please add an objection right with an alternate process (e.g., mitigation plan).
- For attestation, BluePeak requests an initial SGX attestation report and one more report after production cutover. Quarterly snapshots are fine thereafter.
- Please include a short appendix that enumerates the exact telemetry fields Redwood collects by default and the explicit opt-out steps for BluePeak.

If you can update the addendum with those three items, we can circulate to our CISO and Legal for final sign-off.

Thanks — Victor
Chief Contracts Officer
BluePeak Health
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Victor Ramos <victor.ramos@bluepeakhealth.com>, BluePeak Legal <contracts@bluepeakhealth.com>, Serena Holt <serena.holt@bluepeakhealth.com>

- Add an objection right for new subprocessors that could persist PII/PHI and include a mitigation path if invoked.
- Update the attestation schedule to include onboarding and post-cutover attestations.
- Produce a telemetry appendix and opt-out instructions.

I'll circulate a revised addendum and appendix by close of business Thursday and schedule a short review call.

— Kimberly
